BASELINE 86.9230% fuzzy, real 1160, insns T1013/O1019, multiset 34t. BEST 88.6120% fuzzy, real 1180, insns T1013/O1023, multiset 26t. Net +1.689 fuzzy points on a 4052-byte function; sDrawGeom's (1-fuzzy)*size impact fell from 530 to 385.

WHAT CONVERTED AND WHY. The run-26 lever generalised to exactly two of its three siblings. The `data + X + 1` sites that pay are the ones whose shared base is consumed by a NEIGHBOURING array read of the same index (`tmp = pbSwap32(data[next]);` immediately precedes both uv2Ptr and colPtr); the nrmPtr site's neighbour is `tmp = pbSwap32(data[idx]);` but its base is ALSO consumed by the posPtr computation two lines later, so regrouping it re-roots three accesses instead of one and loses.

THE NEW MECHANISM (keep #3), which is the transferable part. At 0x468 our build formed `slwi r0,r29,2 / add r3,r25,r0` for `data[idx]` and then served `data[idx+1]` from it as `lwz r3,4(r3)`; the target instead emits `slwi r0,r31,2 / lwzx r0,r28,r0` for `data[idx]` -- no address register at all -- and a SEPARATE `addi r0,r31,1 / slwi r0,r0,2 / add r3,r28,r0 / lwz r4,0(r3)` for `data[idx+1]`. MWCC forms the address register for `data[idx]` ONLY because a second use exists; naming `idx + 1` in a distinct declared symbol removes that second use and the load collapses to the target's `lwzx`. Our `data[idx]` now matches the target instruction-for-instruction.

REMAINING RESIDUAL: target-only +1 add +1 lfs +1 lwzx +2 mr +1 slwi +1 srwi +1 stfs against ours-only -1 addi -1 lbz -1 lbzx -1 li -4 lwz -1 neg -1 rlwinm -2 stb -3 stw -3 xoris. The single named live mechanism is now the CONVERSE of the one just fixed: at 0x4a8 the TARGET forms `add r3,r28,r0` and serves TWO loads from it -- `lwz r4,0(r3)` for cnt and `lfs f0,8(r3)` for the qv word three elements later -- while we now emit `lwzx` and recompute. Two source forms that should have re-created that share were probed (NEGATIVE #2 and #3 above) and neither reached it, so the axis is closed for spelling; the untried direction is the byte round-trip block at 0x4d4-0x568 approached from the pbSwap32 macro rather than from its argument.
